fragments.text: Target scope approved 16 October 2026.

Spool is an application error tracking and crash reporting product for a US development team replacing Sentry, Datadog Error Tracking, Rollbar or Bugsnag (SmartBear). It serves the complete error-to-repair job: capture web/server/mobile failures, understand impact with source and execution context, route accountable team work, and establish whether a released repair held. PostHog Error Tracking, GlitchTip and Better Stack Error Tracking set the emerging-product comparison; the agent clauses go further through reproduction, tested source repair and live exposure-based verification.
This is the product being built toward. A clause is an obligation, not a claim that it ships today.

The Status rows are maintained by implementation rounds; the clause and acceptance prose was reconciled against main at `3a5e47072e10e637bef632c02b79e7c8f49657a4` (18 October 2026), starting from the 16 October code audit at `9dc0f7ab3083035e56556fe6b773a443a843b3fc`. Changed code since the audit was re-read, including email destination management/testing, delivery issue links, setup/handoff guidance and the later workspace/packet read optimizations; the optimizations preserve the recorded feature boundaries.

`done` means the stated bounded behavior has implementation and checked-in public-door tests; it does not turn local/provider-double results into hosted or commercial acceptance. `partial` names a working subset; `missing` has no implementation proof.

Spool owns error/crash records, release health, error-linked traces/replay, triage and the repair-verification loop. Mobile SDKs, native symbolication, provider applications, billing and heavy sandbox workers are required engineering, not reasons to reduce this scope.

General work planning remains [Vector](https://github.com/just-every/run-vector), and rotations, SMS/voice escalation and incident response remain [Oncall](https://github.com/just-every/run-oncall) or PagerDuty. TRACK-001 and ALERT-002 connect those products; Spool does not recreate their broader job.

For monitoring and observability, see RunEditRun’s sibling [Porthole](https://github.com/just-every/run-porthole). Whole-platform infrastructure APM, general log warehousing, product analytics and model-evaluation suites remain connected services such as Datadog, Splunk and PostHog. CTX-001/002 and AI-007 still require the diagnosis context the error buyer needs; these boundaries do not exclude it.
Scheduled-job and heartbeat monitoring is [Uptime](https://github.com/just-every/run-uptime)'s product.

SDK-024 accepts Sentry SDK check-in envelopes (`capture_checkin`, `@monitor`, `Sentry.withMonitor`) at the DSN and forwards them to the buyer's connected Uptime heartbeat, linking the job's errors to it; without a connection they are counted as unrouted in capability diagnostics, never silently dropped.

Cloudflare is the bounded intake/control plane, not a requirement to run native symbolication, replay processing or persistent sandboxes inside request execution. Use declared isolated worker/storage providers with quotas, custody, portability and erasure coverage; SDK-011's attachment, minidump, profile and replay items and SRC-004's source maps and debug files stream there rather than being held in request memory, and the request-size limits SDK-011 publishes still bind. SDK-002, SDK-011, GOV-002 and AI-002 retain the full obligation.
Production deployment remains the buyer's CI/CD action after review. Telemetry and model suggestions authorize nothing.
AI-003 may write only an approved branch/PR; it never auto-merges or deploys.

Replay/raw requests/identity are opt-in with preview and redaction; no blanket claim of perfect secret removal or legal compliance is made. Health/payment data requires buyer-approved agreements and controls before capture, rather than an implicit assurance.

Local deletion cannot remove already downloaded archives, delivered messages or remote-provider copies; show the limits and partner deletion path. BASE-DATA-003 defines the exact offline-journal and backup limits. No unlimited-ingest or complete-capture claim is permitted; GOV-003 and SRC-004 publish the limited figures a buyer buys (retention, retained volume, sustained intake rate and artifact capacity), and no lower undisclosed cap may stand in for them.
Existing ERR-001 through ERR-010 and BASE-DATA-003 identities remain stable.

**ERR-001 — Bounded admission.** Native version-1 JavaScript, Python and Go exception envelopes require active exact-project ingest credentials, registered release/build identity and bounded fields. Invalid, oversized, volume-limited and conflicting retries have explicit outcomes. Each project admits at most 120 outcomes a minute (`minute_budget`) and retains at most 10,000 events (`retained_event_budget`); over-limit intake returns 429 with `Retry-After` and a counted outcome. GOV-003 carries the target that replaces both limits with its named volume reasons and published sustained rate. Artifact URLs in envelopes are never fetched. Sentry error intake now implements SDK-009's default acceptance with no release or an automatically created release/dist; only its opt-in registered-sequence-only policy requires registration. Native version-1 intake keeps the registered release/build prerequisite. The broader SDK target is SDK-001.

**Acceptance evidence:** Send valid, invalid, oversize, foreign-project and conflicting-retry envelopes through public ingest; inspect the outcome and unchanged rows for refusals. Exceed the per-minute and retained-event limits and confirm the explicit 429, `Retry-After` and counted reason, with no partial rows.

**ERR-002 — Atomic acceptance.** Accepted means a sanitized occurrence, its group aggregate and its local new/regression alert commit atomically. Retry identity is project plus event ID and SHA-256 of canonical original accepted JSON before scrubbing: identical retry never increments, changed raw content conflicts even if its sanitized result matches. Raw bytes are not retained. Group algorithm version and basis remain inspectable.

**Acceptance evidence:** Ingest an event twice, then change its raw secret under the same ID; inspect one occurrence and aggregate increment, one local alert and an explicit conflict without partial rows.

**ERR-003 — Scrub before storage.** Apply the native allowlist, bounded text, query/fragment removal and sensitive-text scrubbing before persistence. Native envelopes contain no headers, cookies, request bodies or personal user identity; the `user` interface that unmodified Sentry SDKs send is governed by SDK-008's project identity policy instead. An optional random installation identifier supports bounded exposure measurement; it is never a name or address. Telemetry, source and notes are untrusted data and cannot authorize execution. The event fields SDK-010 keeps from unmodified Sentry SDKs (frame local variables, SDK-sent source context lines, exception values, tags, contexts, request, extra and thread stacks) pass through these scrubbers and SDK-003's server-side rules before storage, and default secret names are masked inside frame variables. Default protection persists when SDK-003 and CTX-002 introduce opt-in context; those captures require their own field policies and previews. Redaction does not promise removal of arbitrary semantic personal data.
**Acceptance evidence:** Ingest privacy canaries and inspect stored events, issue views, packets, archives and delivery content; common secrets are removed while ordinary diagnostic content survives.

**ERR-004 — Separated authority.** Every private API/document checks the current owner session or its exact ingest, deploy or read-only project grant itself. Cookie writes enforce same origin. Revocation and identity fencing take effect on the next request; confidential maps are never public. Ingest cannot read, deploy can only register releases/upload artifacts and record deployment starts/callbacks, and read-only agent grants cannot mutate. TEAM-001 extends this model to collaborative membership without broadening existing credentials.

**Acceptance evidence:** Call each private transport anonymously and with wrong-scope, foreign-project, revoked and fenced grants; denied writes change no state, and direct map URLs reveal no private bytes.

**ERR-005 — Source map identity.** Private flat Source Map V3 lookup matches project, release, build, debug ID and SHA-256 before presenting original coordinates. Missing, invalid or mismatched maps retain generated frames and a reason. Late uploads never rewrite immutable admission snapshots; current lookup is labeled separately. Lines are one-based, columns zero-based.
A project stores at most 20 flat maps of 256 KiB; indexed (`sections`) maps are refused with a reason and `sourceRoot` is not applied.

**ERR-006 — Audited triage and regression.** Revision-checked open, acknowledged, resolved and suppressed changes are audited. An issue resolved in its current release reopens as a regression on a recurrence in a later release; delayed older-release events cannot invent one. For native version-1 events the order is the registered sequence, never guessed semver; Sentry events follow the project's stated rule in SDK-009, including releases later enriched by registration. SDK-009 implements resolve in the next or a named release and plain Resolve; TEAM-004 inherits resolution from a commit's release. Plain Resolve regresses on the next accepted event in any release. Recognized JavaScript bundle hash suffixes do not split grouping; native anchors and reported frames stay immutable. Corrections retain exact occurrence provenance and reversible fenced apply/undo.

**Acceptance evidence:** Resolve a captured issue, admit its fingerprint in a newer and then older release, and inspect regression identity. Preview/apply/undo split and merge through owner HTTP/UI, reject stale revisions and inspect original membership.

**ERR-007 — Sanitized evidence packet.** A compatible v1 packet exposes issue/lifecycle/grouping, retained release sequence and per-event release/build/environment, generated/original coordinates, immutable diagnostics beside current lookup, links and coded coverage gaps. UTF-8 JSON is bounded to 256 KiB and ten events, removing oldest events first and naming included/available counts even if none fit. It excludes source snippets, sourcesContent and artifact bytes. It carries the latest computed repair observation and newest three owner-recorded repairs, with omitted history named. CLI and stdio MCP keep exact-project read authority and untrusted/no-execution labels; they cause no model egress.

**Acceptance evidence:** Read the same packet through HTTP, CLI and official MCP transport at size/retention/import/loss boundaries; compare projections and verify no secrets, source bytes, writes or cross-project reads.

**ERR-008 — Loss counters and repair observation.** Expose windowed accepted/rejected/budget outcomes, SDK-reported discards by category and reason, and unknown pre-transport loss. Reported discarded errors are a loss input and prevent a quiet feed from proving a repair; other discarded categories do not imply lost errors. Only the owner records revision-checked repair links, scrubbed notes, checks, approval/merge/deploy facts and an exercised-flow record. Links are HTTPS origin/path text and never fetched. Manual repair writes send no notifications or external work. Compute recur/reasoned inconclusive/no-recurrence-after-exercise from stored release sequence, maps, events, exercise and loss; list older-release events separately. Missing exercise, capture, map, exposure or retention yields inconclusive. Never label a quiet feed fixed. AI-004 adds rate-based live proof.
*Status:* done

**ERR-010 — Release gates.** A release must exercise real capture, symbolication, privacy, permissions, persistence and independent restore through the shipped app. Fresh setup has no demo rows. Private flows are accessible and responsive with explicit empty, failure and unavailable states. Source presence, local providers or a green build cannot substitute for hosted, mobile, integration or real-account acceptance. UX-001 and each connector clause specify the expanded product gates.

**Acceptance evidence:** Run the named implemented journeys on the emitted Worker, inspect 1440/390 end states, then qualify each supported runtime/device and configured real provider with a buyer-controlled account.

**OPS-001 — Base commands and native admission.** The public rer command contract uses declared Node/pnpm pins and one setup manifest for terminal/browser. Setup claims or preserves the owner and private settings, stops its temporary app and leaves empty product data; rer dev uses real assets/HMR and private local identity. Local dev grants never authorize deployed entry. Reset is confirmed/contained and preserves source, exports and deployment receipts.
Export/import share Base integrity and inactive empty-target restore.
Deployment dry-run makes no provider request. Managed signed first-owner admission precedes auth dispatch; editor config independently checks the owner and has short expiry/exact-origin CSP.

**Acceptance evidence:** Use public rer install/setup/dev/export/import/reset and deployment dry-run in a fresh checkout and independent destination; preserve existing setup, reject unsafe answer paths and reused managed claims, and deny anonymous/project-grant editor access.

**BASE-DATA-003 — Project and installation-owner erasure.** The owner has count-only preview, typed confirmation bound to the exact current plan, resumable destructive steps and a completion receipt with per-table counts/times and no personal values. Project-root cascade,
anonymized permanent audit,
portability tombstones, source-import custody withdrawal, stale-write fences are preserved,
and project erasure completes within five minutes for a project at today's 10,000-event admission limit.

GOV-003 carries erasure within 15 minutes for 150,000 retained events. Owner self-erasure first transfers authority to a verified successor; it refuses unsupported/ambiguous attribution rather than damaging other people's data.
All current declared tables and outbox copies participate; new capture stores must extend this declaration before release.
**Acceptance evidence:** Run public setup/dev/HTTP/export/import erasure journeys with canaries in every declared store, count-only preview/receipt, wrong-scope/origin/stale denials,
a 10,000-event project erased within 300 seconds,
successor handoff, resumed partial erasure and same/fresh-destination old-archive fences.

**TEAM-001 — Organizations, members and project permissions.** A US development team creates an organization, invites multiple simultaneous members, organizes projects by team, and grants owner/admin, billing (usage, budgets and invoices only), project maintainer, member and read-only access with least privilege. Removal revokes
sessions,
keys and linked service authority; service accounts have explicit project scopes.
Private data, search, exports and integrations obey membership on every transport.

Owner transfer remains available without restricting the organization to one active contributor. Before project role doors ship, enforce project-maintainer authority for SDK-006 inbound filter and GROUP-001 grouping-policy management, replacing the current owner proxy without granting authority outside the member’s project/team scope.

Before this capability ships, every new human/service action, denial, export and notification inherits AUDIT-001: safe permanent actor/subject aliases, time, action and truthful outcome; permissioned organization cursor history/export; append-preserving portability and erasure that removes attribution links without relabeling old facts.
TEAM-001 supplies member deployment authority; the current installation owner acts for REL-001 until then.
**Acceptance evidence:** Invite two teammates and an external read-only collaborator; grant access to disjoint projects, triage concurrently,
remove a member and verify immediate denial across UI, HTTP, SDK-management, CLI and exports.
ALERT-004 alternate-operator responsibility is inherited here: until member roles ship, the installation owner is accountable and configures the alternate destination (default No alternate).
Team roles must preserve an accountable alternate operator, visible broken-destination and overdue follow-up, and nonrecursive deduplication.

ALERT-003 team digests and team snooze inherit this clause before team roles ship: buyer-timezone daily/weekly error digests, required snooze expiry, one durable resumption notice, counted/listed suppressed alerts, and loss/backlog visible through maintenance and quiet hours.
The installation owner acts for these scopes until this clause is implemented.

**TEAM-002 — Accountable assignment and ownership rules.** Assign issues to real members/teams, import GitHub/GitLab CODEOWNERS at the exact linked revision, and define service/path/environment fallback ownership. Preview precedence and unmatched cases, route notifications to the assigned team, and notify assignees of due or unowned work. Work is due when an assigned issue stays unacknowledged past the project's acknowledgment window (set by a maintainer, default 24 hours), when a snooze, suppression or resolve-in-next-release deadline expires, or when a linked delivery ticket's due date passes; unowned work is an issue with no assignee after the project's unowned window. A due notice goes to the assignee, then to the owning team and the ALERT-004 alternate if still unacknowledged. Assignment history survives member departure without conferring access. Rules can be tested and disabled by a maintainer.

**Acceptance evidence:** Connect a repository with overlapping ownership rules, capture matched and unmatched errors, confirm accountable assignment and destination, let an assigned issue pass its acknowledgment window and an unassigned one pass its unowned window and confirm one due notice to the assignee and one unowned notice to the team, then remove the owner and inspect reassignment/history without leaked access.

**TEAM-003 — Collaborative lifecycle and bulk triage.** Teams comment, mention, subscribe (delivery per TEAM-005) and inspect an issue activity timeline; bulk assign, acknowledge, resolve, merge or suppress a selected search result with a preview. Resolution may be plain (Resolve with no release: the next accepted event in any release, or with no release, regresses it, as in Sentry, under SDK-009), in the current release, in the next release, in a named release, or from a commit/PR citation (TEAM-004). The recurrence policy is stated in project settings, with this default: after a release resolution, a same-release repeat does not reopen the issue but is counted on it as "recurred in resolved release" and shown on its timeline; a maintainer can set the project to reopen same-release repeats instead, previewed and audited. Old-release repeats remain separately visible and cannot fabricate newer-release regression; an event with no release after a release resolution follows SDK-009. Suppression (archive) supports reason, forever, expiry/count/affected-user threshold, until escalating (unarchive when volume exceeds the issue's forecast from its own history, with the forecast shown) and snooze, with due follow-up and an audit trail. Every issue has a priority (high, medium or low), set automatically when it opens from its level and history (fatal and error high, warning medium, info and debug low; escalation or regression raises it) and editable by a member. A manual edit sticks against later automatic changes, appears with its actor in the timeline and is audited, and FIND-001 filters, ALERT-001 conditions and TEAM-005 settings can use it. Concurrent edits refuse stale decisions.
*Status:* partial

**TEAM-004 — Issue short IDs and resolution from commits and pull requests.** Every issue has a stable human-readable short ID per project (for example `CHECKOUT-1A3`), shown in the UI, alerts, packets, exports and search; it survives merge/split as an alias. A commit message or a GitHub PR / GitLab MR title or description containing `Fixes`, `Resolves` or `Closes` followed by a short ID (case-insensitive) links that commit or PR to the issue as soon as SRC-002 receives it, visible on the issue timeline. When a release includes the commit, or the merged PR's merge commit, whether the release was registered through REL-001 or SRC-003, or auto-created under SDK-009 and given commits by a later registration or by SDK-009's commit-SHA association, the issue resolves in that release with commit, PR and author recorded. A later occurrence in a newer release reopens it as a regression under ERR-006; an occurrence in an older release cannot. Citations of unknown, other-project or inaccessible short IDs change nothing and appear in the repository link log with the reason.

**Acceptance evidence:** Push a commit and merge a PR that each cite an issue's short ID, register a release containing both through the release API and through `sentry-cli releases set-commits`, and confirm both issues show the link immediately and resolve in that release. Capture each fingerprint in a newer release (regression) and an older one (no regression), and cite another project's short ID (no change, logged). Repeat with an auto-created release named by the merge commit's full SHA and no CI registration, and confirm the issue resolves in it.
SDK-009 automatic full-SHA releases inherit commit/PR association here: resolve cited issues when the linked commit is included, retaining author and citation and protecting older-release recurrence.

Short IDs are `<PREFIX>-<number>`: a per-project counter in Crockford base32 behind a prefix derived once from the project identifier (`<prefix>_2` when taken), never reused or reassigned; an erased project's prefix stays retired.
Migration `0059_short_ids_commit_citations.sql` numbers existing issues in first-seen order, and a restore of an older archive numbers its issues the same way.

Merge moves every short ID of the absorbed issue to the survivor as an alias; split keeps the original's ID and gives the split-out issue the next number; guarded undo restores the recorded mapping, a split-out ID then opening the original where its occurrences returned. Lists, issue view, search, JSON/CSV exports, packets, the agent CLI/MCP, alert email and webhook bodies and digests carry it; packets, issue links and citations accept any short ID or alias in any case.

Until SRC-002 delivers provider pushes, commits reach Spool through the deploy-key release door (`commits`) and deployment door (`includedCommits`), each a bare full SHA (no citation) or `{sha, message, author: {name, email}}` with author kept as sent and the message scrubbed.

A citation links at once to a live issue of the same project and shows on the issue timeline; any other is written to the owner's repository link log with the literal citation, SHA and reason: `unknown` (no issue has the ID), `other_project` (another project's issue) or `inaccessible` (imported history, which a deploy key cannot change). Repeats are idempotent. A cited issue resolves, under SDK-009's named resolution and the project's ordering rule, in the first release that includes the commit: the registered or deployment release, or an auto-created release whose name is the commit's full SHA, which includes it as soon as Spool holds that commit; because a deploy key delivers each commit inside a registration, an auto-created SHA release resolves the issue when it orders before the registered or deployment release that delivers the commit, and one that orders after it — as one created later always does — is associated with the commit while the earlier resolution and its older-release protection stand. The resolution records commit SHA and author, with the PR empty until SRC-002 supplies one, and raises the issue revision so stale owner and bulk decisions are refused.

Commit author and message are personal data shown on owner surfaces only (the issue timeline). Packets, agent CLI/MCP, alert email/webhook bodies and exports carry short ID, citation, release and SHA, adding author and message only after the owner turns on the audited, revision-fenced per-project sharing choice (default off); digests never carry them. A retention cutoff removes author and message from commits received before it and from the alert copies that carried them; project erasure removes every short ID, prefix, commit, link and log row; installation-owner erasure replaces the owner's whole-token identifiers in commit authors and messages. Private archives carry all of it and restore inert, re-running no resolution and sending nothing.

**No release.** An event with no `release` is accepted, grouped and stored with release shown as "none". It counts in issue totals, the issue stream, FIND-001 search (`!has:release`), ALERT-001 conditions and FIND-002 dashboards. It is excluded only from release-scoped figures (release history, per-release counts, SDK-005 adoption and crash-free rates by release, REL-002 comparison), and each of those names how many events had no release.

**Automatic release creation.** The first event or session carrying a `release` (with or without `dist`) that the project has not seen creates that release, as Sentry does, whether the SDK took it from configuration, `SENTRY_RELEASE`, an inferred git commit SHA (Python, Node), the Apple default `CFBundleIdentifier@CFBundleShortVersionString+CFBundleVersion`, the Android, React Native or Flutter default `package@versionName+versionCode`, or a build plugin's injected value. An absent `dist` is its own identity and never means "latest". The release records its first-seen time, first environment and the SDK name and version that created it, and is labeled "auto-created" until CI registers commits, artifacts or a deploy for it. Later registration of the same name through REL-001, `sentry-cli releases new/set-commits/finalize/deploys` or a build plugin (SRC-003) enriches that release and removes the label; it never splits it or changes its first-seen time. A name Sentry's release naming rules refuse (empty, `.`, `..`, `latest`, containing a newline, tab, `/` or `\`, or over 200 characters) creates no release: the event is accepted with release "none" and an "invalid release name" processing note counted per reason. When the name is a full commit SHA that exists in a repository linked through SRC-002, the release is associated with that commit, so suspect commits and TEAM-004 resolution work without a CI step.

**Ordering rule.** Each project shows its release ordering rule in project settings. One transitive total order governs release lists and exports, resolve in the current or next release, TEAM-004 resolution, regression, `release:latest` and REL-002 comparison. Lists use ascending order (a descending view reverses that same order); "latest" is always its final release, never a separately guessed version or registered sequence.

**Default: first seen.** Order all releases by first-seen time, with registration counting as seen when it precedes intake. Equal first-seen times are broken by release name in UTF-8 byte order. Later enrichment never changes first-seen time.

**Optional: semver.** All names that parse as semantic versions, including `package@1.2.3+45` and `1.2.3`, come first, ranked by semver precedence (major, minor, patch and prerelease; build metadata does not affect precedence). Equal precedence is broken by first-seen time, then release name in UTF-8 byte order. Every non-semver name (SHA, date or free text) follows the semver releases, ordered by first-seen time and then release name in UTF-8 byte order. A pair never switches comparison rules based on the other release's name.

**Registered sequence only.** A maintainer can instead choose the stricter rule Spool's native intake uses: order by registered sequence, and refuse a Sentry SDK event or session with no release, or with an unregistered release or `dist`, with its named reason (`missing_release_register_required` or `unregistered_release_or_build`) and a pointer to registration. Each refusal is counted under that reason in project outcomes, BILL-001 usage and the MIG-001 dual run.

**SDK-011 — Sentry intake encodings, published size limits and per-item refusal.** Everything an unmodified Sentry SDK sends with its default transport gets through Spool's intake door. This covers SDK-007's `/envelope/`, `/store/`, `/minidump/`, `/unreal/` and `/security/` endpoints, the SDK-001 tunnel handlers and the first-party ingest subdomain.

**Encodings.** Request bodies are accepted uncompressed or with `Content-Encoding` `gzip`, `deflate`, `br` (Brotli) or `zstd`, and with or without a `Content-Length` (chunked transfer). This includes the Python SDK, which uses Brotli whenever the `brotli` module is installed. Decompression is streamed and stops at the limits below, so a decompression bomb is refused as too large without exhausting memory. An encoding outside this list is refused with 415 naming the encoding, and the refusal is counted.
**Published limits.** Setup, documentation and capability diagnostics publish these limits, each at least equal to Sentry's documented ingest limits:
40 MiB for a compressed request;
200 MiB for an envelope after decompression, including all items;
1 MiB for each event (error or transaction), span, log or metric item;
100 KiB for a check-in item;
4 KiB for a client report item;
50 MiB for a profile item;
10 MiB for a compressed replay item and 100 MiB after decompression;

200 MiB of uncompressed attachments per event, covering attachments, screenshots, view hierarchies, minidumps, Apple crash reports and Unreal crash files, including through `/minidump/` and `/unreal/`;
100 sessions per envelope and 100 session aggregate buckets per `sessions` item.

A maintainer can lower a project's limits, with a preview of affected recent traffic, but cannot raise them above the published figures. Attachment, minidump, profile and replay items stream to the isolated storage named in the boundaries and are never held whole in request memory.

**Per-item refusal.** An item over its limit, or an item that fails to parse, is refused alone with its reason (`item_too_large` or `invalid_item`, with the item type), and the rest of the envelope is accepted. The response and a `client_report`-compatible outcome name the refused item. Only a request over the compressed-request or decompressed-envelope limit is refused whole, with 413 and the limit named.

**Counting.** Each refusal, whether an unsupported encoding, an oversized request, an oversized item or an invalid item, is counted per item type, reason, SDK name and version in project outcomes, SDK-007 capability diagnostics, BILL-001 usage and the MIG-001 dual run. None of them consumes billable quota.

Each source map or source file may be up to 190 MiB, Sentry's only stated per-map limit, with any number of `sources` and mappings within that size. **Formats.** Indexed (`sections`) maps, `sourceRoot`, `sourcesContent`, `ignoreList`/`x_google_ignoreList` (those frames are marked not in-app under GROUP-001), debug IDs (`debugId`/`debug_id`) and release/dist artifact names including `~/` URL prefixes are applied under ERR-005's identity checks, not refused.

Every deleted row gets a Base portability tombstone and stored transfer snapshots are invalidated in each batch. A Sentry-imported project's import-kit custody (its source records and plan entries) and every original export artifact that holds the project are withdrawn in the same import-kit batch as the cascade; other projects in such an artifact keep their native rows, but that artifact's bytes become unavailable to them too. Completion is measured today within five minutes at the current 10,000-event admission cap; the target is GOV-003's published retained volume, within 15 minutes for 150,000 retained events and at no less than 10,000 events a minute above that. Manual retention's visible cutoff, occurrence identities, guarded tombstones and deduplication horizon are unchanged. One erasure runs at a time; an erased project's identifier cannot be reused, since its tombstone would refuse every later archive holding the new project.

Retained scope exceptions, each named in the preview and receipt: the installation owner, claim ledgers and authentication state remain because project erasure preserves installation authority; unrelated projects remain because they lie outside the selected project; project audit entries survive with only their kind and time, their project reference replaced by a random label shared only with the receipt, so a database holder cannot join them back; receipts keep counts and times only; portability tombstones are keyed hashes. Owner self-erasure uses the separate workflow below; project erasure alone does not erase its retained owner. Selective owner erasure remains blocked for shared import custody and unsupported or ambiguous attribution.

Older archives are refused by the installation's restore fence, including archives holding only child rows, and by a fresh destination that first receives the post-erasure archive, or a later archive given with `rer import --journal`. A brand-new store given only an older archive has no later journal and cannot recognize the erasure.

Already downloaded archives, delivered mail, remote provider records, D1 Time Travel and backups, raw database imports and destination secrets (`ALERT_DESTINATIONS`) lie outside the local fence; erasure reports these limits rather than claiming their deletion.
The public-door proof is described in [ACCEPTANCE.md](ACCEPTANCE.md).

Authority moves first. A real successor must accept an ordinary invitation; the first atomic step rechecks both parties' sessions, promotes the successor and retires the predecessor, so exactly one active owner remains and the successor signs in and manages normally. Without a verified successor the operation refuses with a plain reason and changes nothing. A change of authority or captured data before the first destructive commit cancels the untouched operation and releases its write freeze; committed partial deletion keeps the freeze until the final receipt and stays resumable.

Deleted: the owner's operator row, tokens, sessions, external identities, provider session data, step-up challenges, agent and deploy keys they minted, development marks, setup links, pending dependency approvals and their auth outbox mail. Inviting a different successor retires the earlier invitation and invitee. Other people's operators, sessions, grants and captured values are unchanged. Receipts carry counts and times only.

A brand-new store given only an older archive cannot recognize the erasure.
